world.bio: I make talavera-inspired tableware in a shared workshop in Coyoacán, Mexico City. I trained in Puebla for two years with a family workshop, then came back to the city and rented a corner of a shared studio with a kiln. My plates and bowls sell at weekend markets and a few small shops in Roma and Condesa. I am thirty-two and my boyfriend just took a job in Madrid.
skills_assets: Two years of talavera technique in Puebla: tin glaze, cobalt blue, hand-painting with a yucca brush
A secondhand electric kiln, 80 litres, bought three years ago for 28,000 pesos
A wheel and a corner of a shared workshop in Coyoacán, rent 3,500 pesos a month
About 1,200 followers on Instagram, a small mailing list of 300
Stalls at the Sunday market in Parque México once a month

projects.name: Autumn tableware collection
projects.text: I was planning a collection of 40 dinner sets for the Day of the Dead market in late October. Twelve sets are done, the rest are waiting to be fired. Two full firings were lost this month because the kiln controller overshot the target temperature by about 40 degrees, and the glaze ran and fused plates to the shelves. That was around 9,000 pesos of work in the bin.

projects.name: Kiln repair
projects.text: The kiln is a secondhand unit with a digital controller that started to misbehave in August. I ordered a thermocouple and replaced it, and the overshoot got better and then worse again. The technician I called quoted 6,000 pesos for a new controller, and I cannot yet tell if it is the controller or the elements.

projects.name: Collaboration with a cafe
projects.text: A cafe in Roma has asked about 60 mugs for opening in November. I said I would think about it. I do not want to promise anything with a kiln I cannot trust.

notes.text: Opened the kiln on Monday: ruined. The glaze on the blue plates ran like candle wax. I stood there with the lid in my hand and could not even cry. Fed Frida the cat and went to bed at eight.
Carlos, my boyfriend, says it is just a job in Madrid for two years. I said two years is a long time. He said we can visit. We looked at flights. I closed the laptop.

Ran the kiln empty to check the temperature with a pyrometer. It overshot by 38 degrees at the top, then undershot on the way down. I think the controller thinks it is cooler than it is. Written down all the numbers.
Cousin Maru paid for my English class again. I am embarrassed but grateful. In class we practised the words for 'schedule' and 'delay'. My teacher laughed that I am good at the second one.

Market day in Parque México. Sold nine bowls and three plates. A woman asked for a custom set with her grandmother's pattern, a little yellow flower. She showed me a photo of a broken plate. I said I could try. She cried a little. I like days like this.
Frida the cat had kittens? No, I think she is just fat. The vet said she is a boy. We renamed him Frido. He refuses to be renamed.

Talked to my mother on the phone. She asked if I would move to Madrid with Carlos. I said I have a kiln. She said you have a kiln here and you can have a kiln there. She does not understand how these things are tied to a place.
Technician came. Says the relay may be sticking. He wants to replace it, 1,800 pesos. I said do it. He said Friday.
Finished sketches for the grandmother's yellow flower pattern. Tried it on a test tile. It looks like her plate, but a little cleaner. I think she will like it.

messages.text:
Carlos: Madrid is cold already, can you imagine?
Me: I cannot imagine Madrid.
Carlos: Come in December, bring your plates.
Me: If I have plates.

Maru: Class is Tuesday and Thursday, 7 pm. Don't be late this time.
Me: I'm never late.
Maru: You were late last week and the week before.
Me: Fine.

Owner: Hi Lucía, any news about the mugs?
Me: I'm fixing my kiln, I'll know more next week.
Owner: We open on 14 November, so I need a decision by mid-October.

Ernesto: The relay is sticking, I'll bring a new one Friday.
Me: Thank you, how much?
Ernesto: 1,800 with installation, no invoice.

calendar.event: Technician replaces relay on kiln, 11 am
Day of the Dead market in Coyoacán, stall set-up 7 am

relations.about: Architect, just started at a firm in Madrid, calls every night at 10 pm.
Pays for my English classes; works at a bank.
Stray, lives in the workshop courtyard.

constraints: Cannot afford a new kiln this year
Only works with lead-free glazes for tableware
Will not rush firings before the Day of the Dead market
sensitive: Savings around 18,000 pesos, kiln repairs eating them
Feeling torn about Madrid and her own career
